steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: There are more people following than I thought.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: They don't necessarily think that they have a better chance with you.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I understand.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: They don't stand behind me because they trust me. They just don't have any other choice.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Footsteps are convincing. The more people join us, the less others will hesitate. When we...

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: When we and Her Royal Highness arrive at the blockade, there will be more cannon fodder?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I'll be standing at the fore, Cador.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Hey, what's that in the sky?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: The Sarkaz airship... they're taking off.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: This is our—

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: No, that's—
The crowd falls silent, gazing up at the airship above.
In their eyes is reflected the eerie purple flame, slowly falling towards the ground.
The cold flame impacts the earth, the sparks flying onto the fleeing crowd, as though they had a mind of their own.
The fire spreads uncontrollably, instantly engulfing the refugees.
They fall to the ground, screaming.
Then, their lifeless bodies rise from the fire, the purple flame of desire burning in their eyes.
Dead silence.
All present bore witness to the 'miracle'.

steps.name: Frightened Refugee
steps.text: A-Another of those devils' tricks?

steps.name: Frightened Refugee
steps.text: They won't even let us die?
The rain of purple fire descends, like the mantle of death itself.
Fear spreads in the crowd. The silence is broken, replaced by panic.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Get away from the fire! Hurry!

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: The houses by the street are burning.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Do you see that, Siege?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: This purple fire is beyond the Sarkaz.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I've heard stories of the dead coming back to life... stories about a Draco.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: The leader of Dublinn. The red dragon of avarice... she's here. Her flame descends upon us.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: She hides her ambition no more, Siege.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I don't care who she is.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: All I care is that we need to run. Now.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Look out!

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Looks like age has not taught you patience.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Why do you fear my fire, if you're so eager to fight me?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Or have you forsaken the intelligence that you were so proud of, once you began serving the Regent?

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Interesting, little Draco, your fire... very interesting.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: If you know about our existence, then you know that this vessel is simply one of our innumerable fragments.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: This is simply a little warning, delivered in passing. You are not in our field of view.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Your soul is too shallow, too barren. You do not even attempt to hide the flame of ambition, the desire for power in your eyes.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Unlike the Banshee whom we are speaking to, even now, we are not even interested in asking any questions of you.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: I have no need to hide. My fire burns away all, as it does now.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: I can't wait until the cluster of Damazti kneels before me in fire.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Do you hear the sound of screaming beneath your feet, hatchling?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: I lead them. They adore me.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: This is my duty. You do not understand, ancient wanderer.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Many years ago, the country beneath our feet was not the farce it is today. We met a Draco in southern Victoria, one as young as you are now.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: 'I lead them. They adore me.' He said the same words, before his death in battle.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: His brood submitted to the empire's glow, whether it was those who made peace with the Aslan, or you.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: How do you think you compare to your conquering forefathers?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: You're not worthy to speak of my kin's suffering.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: And I'm not worthy to speak of the red dragon who wrote the history of Tara.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: But the beautiful memories that you speak of have left Tara a long time ago.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: The old Draco kings were no greater than we are. We sought fairness. He made his choice, and I made mine.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: You, long-lived, you boast of the seasons that you've seen, the scope of your knowledge.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: But the wealth that you are so proud of has not changed your life in the slightest. How pathetic.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Observe and seek. That is all you have in all your years, no?

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: Neither of us see the other as a welcome guest. Why not end this pointless argument?

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Thank you, little Draco, for making this chore somewhat interesting.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: You'll remember me, Damazti.

steps.name: Eblana
steps.text: There will be a chapter with my name on it in your long and winding memory.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: The fire outside...

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Now's no time to stare. Pack up and let's catch up with... Morgan?

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Do you regret what you said to Vina?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: I don't know why. It just came out... I didn't mean to blame her.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: I wanted someone to tell me that the nightmare was over, that everything would get better. That someone used to be Vina.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Remember this tape? You spent a pretty penny to get it from McClaren.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Bastard lied to me, said it was limited edition and worth a lot.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: He wasn't wrong. How many times did you watch it with Vina on the sofa? Ten? Twenty?

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Tell you what. Grab it, and we'll all watch it for the twenty-first time when we get out of here and find our new hideout. How about that?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: She never changed, did she?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: It was Norport that changed.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Speaking of video... there's someone I haven't notified.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: You go first. Tell Vina I'll catch up soon.
The lights by the streets of Norport have gone out. Only the purple flames spreading through the city light Baird's path.
Burning silhouettes stare blankly at the sky, listening to the call of 'The Leader.'
But the dark night conceals the airship in the sky. Not even the purple flames reaching towards the skies could reveal it.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Damn it, what are those people... those things looking at?

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: I have to find McClaren, meet up with Vina. It's not safe here. I think he lives over here...

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: It's too dark. Should have brought my flashlight.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: His neon sign used to stay lit all night.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Those burning... things... had better not jump me like those movie monsters.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Third from the left... third from the left... there!

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: McClaren!

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: The next house is burning! We have to go!
No one answers Baird in the darkness. All she hears is the crackling of fire on wood.
Baird presses her ear against the gap, and hears the faint chattering of teeth and agitated breathing echo in the empty house.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: McClaren! Thank heavens you're alive.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Oh yeah, Morgan said he's deaf...

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: I need a pen... I've got one here in my pocket!

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: 'It's not safe here. We need to go.'

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: 'I'm Baird. Take the planks down.'

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Read the note, bloody hell, do you see it or not?!

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: There's no time. I need to go in...

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: It's okay, McClaren. I just need to pry your windows open.
Baird widens the gap in the planks using her knife, then tries to pry them open with the handle.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Almost there, almost there!

steps.name: McClaren
steps.text: (Go away...)

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Are you talking? I can't hear you. The planks aren't that tough. Hang in there!

steps.name: McClaren
steps.text: (Get away from me... get away from me...)

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: What are you saying? Damn, the fire's spreading quickly.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Hurry... hurry...

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Last two. Do you see me, McClaren?

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: 'Come over to the door.' The fire's spreading. We're out of time!

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Look this way! Isn't it clear enough?

steps.name: McClaren
steps.text: (Go away... get away from me...)

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Stand back. I'll kick the last planks in.

steps.name: McClaren
steps.text: Stay away!!!
A silver flash. Baird takes a step back, touches her cheek, and finds it wet with a warm liquid.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: What the...?

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: McClaren...
The familiar video shop owner stands behind the door.
The blood flowing from his ears lies dried on his neck. Originium crystals cover a large part of his ears. Morgan was right. He has likely gone deaf.
He's muttering at the only light in the room, oblivious to everything else.
Otherwise, he would not have been so frightened when he saw that it was her standing outside, would not have swung his knife.
Or perhaps not.
He would have done so, no matter who opened the door.
The calamity outside has taken his hearing, and almost everything else he had. He stands alone with his knife, only a few fragile planks between the world and the last bit of food he has.

steps.name: McClaren
steps.text: This is mine... I have nothing left...

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: McClaren...

steps.name: McClaren
steps.text: I want to live... please... I just want to live. I've given you everything else...

steps.name: McClaren
steps.text: What do you still want from me?

steps.name: McClaren
steps.text: (This is mine...)

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Look at me, McClaren. It's Baird. I'll take care of you.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Put down your knife. Take my hand.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: 'Put down your knife.' Can you read it?

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: The fire is spreading. We've no time.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Right, just like that. I'll come over slowly. No need to be scared.
Finally, Baird sees the once-familiar video shop owner in his entirety.
She finds that it is not a lamp that illuminates the room, but the tiny projector that they spent countless days and nights with.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: I'll take your hand and help you up.

steps.name: McClaren
steps.text: (I want to live...)

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: You will. We all will.
Baird touches the feeble arm. Her heart skips a beat at the solidness of the Originium crystals beneath the soft muscles.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: It's ok. We'll all live. You'll have a new video shop, and I'll have a new gym.

steps.name: McClaren
steps.text: (I want to live...)

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Relax... now I'm going to take your knife. You're safe. You don't need it.

steps.name: McClaren
steps.text: Thank you... thank you...
She reaches out slowly to the knife that McClaren is holding. There is a little bump under his clothes, the last food that McClaren has left.
Baird takes McClaren's knife. The muscles of the trembling man relax for the first time in many days.
Baird sees an emotion other than fear in the man's eyes. Perhaps he has recognized her.
The thing in the bump falls out from under his clothes. It's an empty can.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: We can go now.

steps.name: McClaren
steps.text: (That's mine...)
Baird exhales and bends down to pick up the empty can.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: But this is emp—
Baird feels a sharp pain in her midsection. The knife that should have been in her hand is now halfway inside her. McClaren was the one who seized her hand.

steps.name: McClaren
steps.text: It's mine! Mine!

steps.name: McClaren
steps.text: Mine...

steps.name: McClaren
steps.text: (I'll live. You said you'll leave me food...)

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: I... ugh...
He stumbles towards Baird and snatches away the meaningless, empty can.

steps.name: McClaren
steps.text: (I'll live. I'll protect myself...)
His knife is now inside Baird. He anxiously looks for a new weapon.
He sees Baird's butterfly knife, his delirious eyes reflected in the cold blade.
Baird has had the knife for a long time.
When the members of the Glasgow Gang were just children, Baird bought it at the flea market at a discount, and never let it leave her side.
It has seen many battles, many celebrations with her. It was not particularly valuable, nor did Baird particularly treasure it. It just became a habit.
McClaren's struggle was feeble. That one stab took almost all the strength he had left.
But Baird found that she could not fight back.
McClaren gasps a few times and pulls with what strength he has left. The blade almost pierces his neck.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Careful! Don't... hurt yourself.
Baird cannot lift her arm. She releases the knife.
The man takes the weapon, cradles the can, and stumbles into the light of the inferno outside.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Haha, haha.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: It hurts... gotta get Hannah to wrap it up... I hope she learned how to do it gently in her time out there.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: *cough* *cough*...

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Ugh... I can hardly stand...

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: McClaren, you bastard... I don't remember owing you any money...

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: Leastwise, I can't remember.

steps.name: Baird
steps.text: I have to catch up to them... Vina'll worry...

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: That's probably the last group that would follow us.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: The flames are burning fierce!

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Looks like we made it, Doctor.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Yes... I'm fine.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Finally. Hurry, while—

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Seems like the airship taking off was enough to get the dukes' attention.

options: Is that the Duke of Windermere's forces?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I don't know and I have no time to care.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: We need to go, Siege!

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: We can't wait for the dukes and the Sarkaz to have it out—

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: No! Baird's not here yet!

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Two minutes. No, one. Baird runs fast.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: You see those walking carcasses on the street? Who knows if they don't want a piece of us, even if we got away from the bombing and the fire.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: We have no time!

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Where's Baird, Morgan?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: She went to look for the video shop owner. It's on the far side...

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: What's more important to you, your subjects or your gang?

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: That's the question you'll need to answer, sooner or later.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Where are you going, Cador?

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: I'm just a Glasgow punk. I don't need to think about the things that you have to, 'Your Highness'.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: Baird's one of my own. I've got to take care of her.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: I look forward to seeing whether you'll keep your promise, and always stand at the fore of these people.

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: ...I hope you do.
Cador squeezes past the silent crowd and goes back into the blockade area.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Let me go, Morgan! Say something, Vina!

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Hannah! Is that McClaren? There at the end of the line... he just joined it!
Cador stops in his tracks.
The cowering man at the end of the line looks around gingerly, then disappears into the crowd.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: McClaren...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: It's him! Baird's caught up!

steps.name: Cador
steps.text: That thing in his hand—

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Baird should be around here. Weren't they together? Wait... how did McClaren end up with Baird's knife?
Morgan finds the answer.
She finds it in the bloodstains on the knife in the video shop owner's hand, and in Vina's eyes before she turned away.
Tears rush into her eyes, but she cannot wipe them away. She needs both her hands to stop Indra from trying to squeeze past the crowd.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Let me go, Morgan, or I'll sock you!

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: (You saw it, Vina...)

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: (Baird—)
Strength. Vina has never wanted it so much.
A little strength. A lot of strength. The strength of anger. The strength of sorrow.
Anything.
Anything to shatter all that lies before her, anything to make things right again.
Even just a little bit—
Even if it was just enough for her to turn around, to find a friend that she has not yet had the time to catch up with.
Even if...
Kyngasycath is heavy in her hands, almost immovable.
Nothing. There is nothing.

steps.name: Nervous Citizen
steps.text: Your Royal Highness... are we not going?

steps.name: Nervous Citizen
steps.text: You will take us away from here, yes?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Don't call me 'Your Highness'. I'm not anybody's Highness.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I'm just... no, never mind.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Stay at your post, Indra!

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: We break the walls now.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: You'll leave Baird behind?! After we've already done so once?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I understand.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: And I know she would not willingly part with us again.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Unless... she had no choice.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: As we do not.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Why did we come back to Norport, then?!

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Maybe coming back was more than just about coming back, the moment that we stepped foot on the soil of our home...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Let go of Hannah, Morgan. Have some faith in the Glasgow Gang.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: We're no wimps.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Remember how we fought our battles when we were little?

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Vina...

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: For the Glasgow Gang!

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: For the Glasgow Gang!

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Bastards... wait for us, Baird...

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: For the Glasgow Gang!
The walls that block the escape of the people of Norport lie just before them, but there are no longer Sarkaz bows and guns on it.
Freedom is in sight. The oppressed raise their hands high and push forth.
Siege raises Kyngasycath high again. It is still just a piece of metal, not a single sheen to it.
She does not remember whether she swung it. Perhaps it is just the result of countless hands pushing at the same time. The wall falls.
